mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops as specified but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production increases and housing starts rise, it indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies rise but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates during a monetary easing cycle increase liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation as indicated by CPI suggests reduced cost pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in retail sales indicates strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases as specified but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases and unemployment decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies improve but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates in a tightening cycle may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises as specified but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
